Team —

We need a concise playbook for the Acme on-prem pilot next week covering two items that have been tripping us up in previous pilots:

1) Sidecar certificate pinning and rotation model (how the sidecar validates the platform cert, CSR flow, rotation window)
2) Split-resolver / DNS fallback behavior for clients in isolated customer networks (how sidecar resolves private FQDNs vs public, what to do when resolver cannot reach upstream)

High-level constraints from Acme (they cc'd Ellie): they will require pinned validation of the server cert chain (no blind trust of platform CA) and they run a restrictive egress policy — so OCSP/responder calls may need relay or an internal responder.

I've attached a sample CSR/subjectAltName layout and a quick diagram for DNS fallback. Can each of you weigh in with a brief recommendation we can lock into the runbook by EOD? Specifically:

- Karthik: recommended sidecar verification (pinning approach + TTLs + rotation steps)
- Grace: operational checks and monitoring we should add to Console (alerts, token-level traces to correlate cert errors)
- Ben: suggested changes to onboarding checklist so SRE/customer success collects necessary DNS/ocsp endpoints and HSM/KMS rotation windows up front

Goal: one-page playbook we can hand to Acme's infra team and a short internal appendix with troubleshooting steps.

Thanks —

On Mon, May 4, 2026 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> We need a concise playbook for the Acme on-prem pilot next week covering two items...

Quick technical response / proposed defaults:

1) Sidecar cert validation & pinning\- Approach: enforce public-key pinning of the leaf certificate (SPKI pin) + require signed chain anchored to a customer-provided intermediate when they want PKI separation. This lets the sidecar verify identity without hardcoding our internal CA roots.
  - Pin format: base64(SHA256(spki)) stored in sidecar config (rotations accept an array to allow overlap).
  - Rotation window: "dual-pin" overlap period of 72 hours for leaf rotations, 14 days for intermediate swaps.
  - CSR flow: sidecar can generate CSR locally and push to Redwood private CA (or accept customer-signed leaf). Provide sample CSR in attachment.
  - Failure mode: if pin mismatch -> reject and emit a high-severity alert; fallback to an "out-of-band" manual approval channel (required for first-time rollout).

2) DNS split-resolver & fallback\- Approach: prefer customer resolver for private zones; if NXDOMAIN or timeouts persist for T1 = 500ms x 3 retries, fall back to an internal split-resolver via configured tunnel (not public recursive). Avoid public resolver fallback unless customer explicitly permits.
  - Algorithm: attempt customer resolver -> if SERVFAIL/timeout, query configured internal proxy resolver (over mTLS) -> if still unresolved, surface a clear SRE diagnostic and return failure to client.
  - Cache behavior: maintain a short negative cache (30s) to avoid flip-flopping. Positive records respect TTL but cap to 5m for critical endpoint records during onboarding.

OCSP / stapling considerations\- Since Acme restricts egress, we should support two modes: (A) sidecar staples OCSP responses obtained from an internal OCSP relay (preferred), (B) sidecar validates issuer CRLs/OCSP via an internal mirror (offline) that the customer provides. We need to document how to configure each mode.

I'll draft the one‑pager with these defaults and a short appendix of commands to reproduce test failures.

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick draft. A few Acme constraints to call out so the playbook matches our security team expectations:

* We will provide our own issuing intermediate and do not allow Redwood to mint roots in our environment. Intermediate rotation is on a 90-day cadence and must be provable via signed rotation manifest.
* OCSP stapling by the sidecar is acceptable only if the stapled response is served from an internal OCSP responder we host behind our resolver. We cannot allow outbound OCSP queries to public responders.
* DNS fallback to an external resolver is a no-go. If your internal proxy resolver is used it must authenticate via mTLS and present a CN that we can pin on our side.
* For the first rollout we need a diagnostic mode where the sidecar logs full DNS resolver traces to a temporary S3 bucket we control (30 day retention) so our NetOps can validate behavior.

We've attached a short PDF summarizing OCSP expectations (acme-ocsp-requirements.pdf). We'll also provide the intermediate cert and the rotation manifest ahead of the pilot.
